items.title: Electron desktop architecture spike
items.description: Implement the common desktop benchmark fixture as a disposable Electron prototype and record the evidence needed for framework selection.
acceptance_criteria: The prototype completes the shared benchmark scenario without changing its application contract or measurement procedure
Packaging, startup, idle and active resource use, accessibility, automated testing, worker failure and reconnect behavior, and permission surface are measured
The implementation records TypeScript and Electron learning demands, boundary complexity, platform constraints, and significant framework-specific code
The spike is clearly isolated from production code and can be discarded after the framework decision
Findings use the common evidence template and include reproducible build and benchmark instructions
items.source: RFC-0004 Expected Follow-Up Tickets: Electron architecture spike
items.notes: Completed 2026-08-18. The disposable Electron prototype passes BTN-37's unchanged scenario and validator through its packaged main/preload/renderer path. Evidence records a 774.39 ms median packaged scenario, 370,696,192-byte median idle working set, four-process idle model, 365,521,443-byte unpacked package and 145,435,393-byte ZIP, a mechanically narrowed renderer, ambient Node main-process authority, and the largest boundary/toolchain surface of the candidates. Clean-machine launch, active-memory sampling, native screen-reader inspection, and real-worker crash recovery were unavailable and remain recorded limitations. Focused Python and Node contract validation pass.

items.title: Desktop framework selection ADR
items.description: Compare the three framework spikes using their common evidence and record the selected production desktop framework in an accepted ADR.
acceptance_criteria: The ADR compares Tauri, PySide6, and Electron against every measurement category defined by the shared fixture
Claims are traceable to reproducible spike evidence and distinguish measurements from judgment
The decision considers human and machine learning, maintainability, application-boundary integrity, packaging, platform support, accessibility, testing, recovery, security, and resource cost
The ADR selects one production framework or explicitly records why more bounded evidence is required
Disposable spike code is not silently promoted into production without reconciliation against Battalion architecture and repository standards
items.source: RFC-0004 Expected Follow-Up Tickets: Desktop framework ADR
items.notes: Completed 2026-08-18. ADR-0022 accepts PySide6 with Qt Widgets for production desktop presentation after comparing all nine BTN-37 evidence categories across Tauri, PySide6, and Electron. PySide6 had the fastest median completed scenario (484.99 ms), lowest median idle working set (82,890,752 bytes), one-process presentation model, and simplest fit with Battalion's Python application boundary. The decision also records Tauri's stronger packaging, renderer-capability, recovery, and measured accessibility results. BTN-42 must close PySide6's clean-machine packaging, native accessibility, worker-failure, restart, and ambient-authority risks; disposable spike code is not production code.

items.title: Read-only desktop operator console
items.description: Deliver the first production desktop vertical slice for browsing Work, History, execution evidence, provenance, token and cost usage, and the Intel library without state-changing controls.
acceptance_criteria: The selected desktop framework presents project and ticket Work views, run History, and detailed node-attempt inspection through the shared application boundary
Execution detail displays model, role, phase, prompt version and hash, Git revision and dirty-state limitations, bounded context provenance, artifacts, verification, tokens, and cost source semantics
The Intel library and persisted Recon candidates are discoverable without allowing the read-only slice to promote, reject, resume, or mutate them
Active runs update through the live observation contract and recover authoritative state after client restart or disconnect
Empty, loading, malformed, legacy, unknown-cost, crashed-worker, and inaccessible-project states are explicitly represented and tested
The UI never invokes LangGraph or edits persisted RunState directly
items.source: RFC-0004 Expected Follow-Up Tickets: Read-only operator console
items.notes: Completed 2026-08-20. The production PySide6 Qt Widgets client presents Work, History, detailed execution evidence, accepted Intel, and persisted Recon candidates exclusively through battalion.application read queries. It renders prompt, Git, bounded-context, artifact, verification, token, sourced-cost, legacy, missing, malformed, inaccessible, loading, empty, crashed-worker, and unknown-cost semantics; state-changing controls are absent and mechanically guarded. Durable-first reconnect is tested before post-barrier observations, including visible UI refresh after state checkpoints and a real subprocess death recovered as a crashed worker. Native Windows UI Automation exposed 25 named and 7 keyboard-focusable elements on the Work surface, including Work/History/Intel navigation; Qt keyboard tests traverse every destination. The standalone build produced a 70-file, 143,124,648-byte distribution, launched from an unrelated clean project with exit code 0, and recorded a five-second packaged idle sample of 103,440,384 working-set bytes and 51,920,896 private bytes. Full offline validation: 404 tests passed. The disposable BTN-39 spike remains separate production evidence.

items.title: Desktop human-action surfaces
items.description: Add canonical interrupt resolution and Recon candidate review to the desktop client, followed by typed next-attempt Correction and Design decision context.
acceptance_criteria: Interrupt resolution and resume use the same application operations and graph-control path as the CLI
Recon candidates can be reviewed, promoted, or rejected through canonical Intel workflows without mutating immutable candidate evidence
Correction targets Driver RED, Driver GREEN, or Refactorer, while Design decision targets Architect
Interventions are queued as bounded context for the next attempt and do not steer an in-flight model generation
Reviewer-targeted intervention, Reviewer verdict override, and manual checkpoint override are not introduced
Every human action records actor, time, target, disposition, and resulting durable state and is covered by authorization and failure-path tests
items.source: RFC-0004 Expected Follow-Up Tickets: Human-action surfaces
items.notes: Completed 2026-08-20. ADR-0023 records the accepted authority and delivery contract. Typed application operations now resolve interrupts through the canonical resume path, review immutable Recon candidates through the existing audited workflow, and queue bounded Corrections or Design decisions for one exact next node attempt with durable pre-generation association and complete human-action evidence. Accessible PySide6 controls expose those operations without Reviewer intervention, verdict override, manual checkpoint override, or in-flight steering. Authorization and failure paths are covered by the 418-test offline suite. Native validation confirmed that the split lightweight desktop build completed quickly and the independent graph/provider worker build completed without hanging; both apply Nuitka pytest anti-bloat policy and emit compilation reports.

items.title: History search and model-role analytics projections
items.description: Build rebuildable projections for run-history search and descriptive model-by-role evidence without turning correlation into automated model selection claims.
acceptance_criteria: Operators can search run history across tickets, summaries, roles, models, phases, outcomes, interrupts, verification, artifacts, and Intel references using rebuildable derived indexes
Search indexes can be deleted and reconstructed from canonical persisted evidence without data loss
Analytics compare model-role observations using transparent measures such as attempts, outcomes, review results, tokens, cost, duration, and available ticket characteristics
Unknown and incomparable evidence is displayed explicitly; small samples and confounding ticket characteristics are not presented as effectiveness conclusions
No automatic model router, hidden score, or replacement source of truth is introduced
Projection versioning, migration, filtering, and representative search and aggregation behavior are tested
items.source: RFC-0004 Expected Follow-Up Tickets: Search and analytics projections
items.notes: Objective ticket characteristics and any later semantic-search approach should emerge from accumulated usage evidence. This ticket begins with descriptive, rebuildable projections.

items.title: Specifier role architecture RFC
items.description: Decide whether Battalion should add a Specifier role and define the human-reviewed specification artifact, authority boundary, lifecycle, and graph relationship before any implementation.
acceptance_criteria: The RFC compares keeping specification authoring outside Battalion, running a separate pre-run workflow, and adding a graph phase without assuming that a new role is required
The proposed specification artifact, provenance, persistence owner, versioning, and relationship to canonical ticket identity are explicit
Human review, edit, acceptance, rejection, cancellation, ambiguity, and conflicting-source behavior are defined without allowing generated product decisions to become authoritative silently
Any proposed role has exact inputs, outputs, write scope, tools, prompt contract, model policy, context budget, execution evidence, cost semantics, and failure behavior
Graph placement, run identity, Architect handoff, checkpoints, interrupts, resume behavior, and application operations are reconciled with existing contracts
Representative workflow evidence and operator-correction measures support the decision, and accepted implementation work is split into separate tickets with required specification and ADR updates
items.source: README Future Architecture Planning; docs/future/specifier-role.md
items.notes: Planning only. The ticket may reject a Specifier role or keep it outside the execution graph; no role, prompt, state, or graph implementation is authorized.

items.title: Plugin architecture and integration lifecycle RFC
items.description: Specify permissioned extension points and a complete plugin lifecycle without weakening write scopes, application policy, secret handling, offline operation, or repository sources of truth.
acceptance_criteria: The RFC defines a minimal extension-point taxonomy and explicitly identifies graph, state, interrupt, scope, and human-decision boundaries that plugins cannot replace
Manifest identity, provenance, versioning, compatibility, dependencies, discovery, installation, enablement, configuration, update, disablement, removal, and retained-data behavior are specified
Filesystem, process, network, credential, model, ticket, and application-operation capabilities require explicit least-authority grants with inspectable defaults
Secret ownership, redaction, context exclusion, audit evidence, isolation, timeout, cancellation, crash recovery, and offline degradation semantics are defined
The threat model covers malicious, stale, compromised, over-privileged, incompatible, and unavailable plugins plus source-of-truth conflicts and duplicate remote mutation
A disposable integration scenario validates the proposed boundary, and accepted runtime, SDK, packaging, marketplace, and example integration work is split into separate tickets and ADRs
items.source: README Future Architecture Planning; docs/future/plugin-architecture.md
items.notes: Planning only. Live JIRA, MCP, repository, model-provider, or other integrations remain examples rather than accepted implementation scope.

items.title: Severity-based review and Guardian role RFC
items.description: Determine whether severity-based review belongs in existing Reviewer and interrupt policy or warrants a distinct Guardian role with a separate evidence and authority boundary.
acceptance_criteria: The RFC compares no new behavior, focused mechanical tooling, Reviewer policy specialization, and a distinct Guardian role without assuming that another graph node is beneficial
Objective trigger inputs, severity taxonomy, classification ownership, uncertainty, false positives, and human correction behavior are defined
Any proposed role has distinct responsibilities, inputs, outputs, prompt contract, model policy, write scope, durable evidence, and pass, finding, retry, failure, and cancellation semantics
Graph placement and every transition are reconciled with RED, GREEN, refactor, Reviewer, interrupt, manual-checkpoint, human-resolution, and resume contracts
Representative low- and high-impact cases compare finding quality, duplicate feedback, operator burden, explainability, latency, cost, and failure modes
The RFC records a no-role, policy-only, or bounded-role decision and splits accepted graph, state, prompt, interrupt, UI, test, specification, and ADR work into separate tickets
items.source: README Future Architecture Planning; docs/future/guardian-role.md
items.notes: Planning only. Model-assigned severity is not authoritative, and no Guardian node or new checkpoint is accepted by this ticket's creation.

items.title: Bounded self-modification safety and evidence RFC
items.description: Define whether and how Battalion may propose changes to its own graph and role definitions through isolated, reviewable, human-authorized engineering workflows without runtime self-editing or self-approval.
acceptance_criteria: The RFC defines self-modification as version-controlled change proposals and explicitly forbids same-run mutation, automatic approval, merge, deployment, permission expansion, or protection bypass

A threat model covers authority escalation, prompt or review tampering, compromised state, recursive execution, stale bases, malicious changes, validation evasion, secret exposure, and rollback failure
Human checkpoints for objective, architecture, scope, validation, acceptance, merge, rollout, rollback, and mechanical stop are explicit and cannot be satisfied solely by the proposing execution

Isolation between the running trusted Battalion instance and candidate worktree or environment is defined together with provenance for objectives, plans, prompts, models, tools, diffs, tests, reviews, decisions, and revisions

A staged evidence plan begins with read-only analysis and disposable patch proposals and includes rejection, failed validation, protected-surface edits, independent review, recovery, budget, recursion, and stop conditions
The RFC makes explicit go, no-go, and stop decisions for each stage, may reject the capability entirely, and requires separate human-approved tickets for every experiment or implementation
items.source: README Future Architecture Planning; docs/future/self-modification.md
items.notes: Long-term research planning only. Dogfooding does not authorize autonomous self-editing, and this ticket must not change runtime graph, role, scope, interrupt, merge, or deployment authority.

items.title: Pluggable repository quality gates and anti-slop evaluation
items.description: Decide how deterministic repository quality checks such as linters should participate in Battalion runs, and validate the proposed boundary with dmmulroy/anti-slop as a TypeScript/JavaScript case study without assuming that linting belongs in the plugin architecture.
acceptance_criteria: The design compares core-owned quality gates, permissioned plugins defined by BTN-46, and repository-owned CI or command hooks, and records why the selected boundary preserves one application and graph policy authority

A language-neutral quality-gate contract defines discovery, configuration, working directory, inputs, command or API invocation, structured findings, exit semantics, timeouts, cancellation, version compatibility, and unavailable-tool behavior

Execution placement relative to Driver RED/GREEN, Reviewer clean-tree verification, refactoring, interrupts, resume, and human override is explicit, with durable provenance for tool identity, version, configuration, findings, and disposition
Filesystem, process, network, dependency-installation, and configuration-write capabilities remain least-authority grants and cannot broaden node write scopes or silently mutate the target repository

A disposable TypeScript/JavaScript fixture evaluates anti-slop and a representative Python check evaluates whether the contract is genuinely language-neutral, including pass, finding, malformed-output, missing-tool, timeout, and false-positive scenarios

The decision identifies which findings are advisory versus blocking, documents the operator correction path, and splits any accepted runtime, plugin SDK, bundled checker, UI, specification, ADR, and test work into separate tickets
items.source: User backlog request 2026-08-20; github.com/dmmulroy/anti-slop; BTN-46
items.notes: Planning and disposable evaluation only. anti-slop is an opinionated vendored Oxlint rule set for TypeScript and JavaScript, not a Battalion dependency or a language-neutral contract. This ticket does not authorize a plugin loader, automatic dependency installation, a new graph checkpoint, or blocker policy.

items.title: Repository status badges and README trust signals
items.description: Add a compact, accessible badge row to the Battalion README that communicates verifiable repository health and project entry points without making unsupported package, service, or contribution claims.
acceptance_criteria: The README begins with a compact badge row covering automated test status, supported Python version, MIT license, published documentation, and selected repository or contribution signals that are useful to prospective users and contributors

The test-status badge is backed by a GitHub Actions workflow that installs declared development dependencies and runs the credential-independent test suite on supported Python, with no live provider calls
Every badge has meaningful alt text, links to the corresponding workflow, documentation, license, contribution guidance, or repository page, and renders legibly on GitHub in light and dark themes

Dynamic badges report actual public repository state; package-registry, container-registry, API-access, community-service, or 'PRs welcome' badges are included only when their target and claim are valid for Battalion
Badge URLs and README rendering are covered by focused validation, and the published Pages staging build is checked so the README-derived landing page has no broken badge or destination links
The final badge set stays visually restrained and documents any omitted candidates, including their missing prerequisite or relevance concern
items.source: User backlog request 2026-08-20; reference badge image
items.notes: The reference image suggests CI, stars, license, contribution, container-registry, API, and DeepWiki-style badges. It is visual inspiration rather than proof that Battalion currently has those services. Do not add decorative, stale, or unverifiable badges.

items.title: Zero-cost inference and model-endpoint architecture RFC
items.description: Define Battalion's inference-target model for local and zero-cost remote inference without replacing LiteLLM, weakening model-diversity guarantees, or allowing an external router to silently own Battalion's role or model-selection policy.
acceptance_criteria: The RFC distinguishes requested model, resolved model, provider, backend or endpoint, and cost policy instead of treating one LiteLLM model string as the complete inference identity

Local inference through Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, or another OpenAI-compatible endpoint and remote inference through FreeLLMAPI are evaluated as optional inference sources behind the existing LiteLLM boundary

The RFC defines local-only, free-only, and explicitly configured paid-capable policy semantics, including classification ownership, evidence requirements, and behavior when monetary cost or free-tier status is unknown

BTN-14 model diversity remains mechanically meaningful behind proxies and routers; opaque aliases that may resolve Driver and Reviewer to the same underlying model cannot silently satisfy the constraint
Credential, endpoint URL, local or remote classification, secret, connectivity validation, failure, retry, failover, offline degradation, and upstream terms-of-service responsibilities are explicit

FreeLLMAPI remains optional infrastructure rather than a replacement for Battalion policy, and its presence alone is not evidence that every routed request is zero-cost, stable, or production-suitable
BTN-35 semantics remain intact so absent monetary evidence is recorded as unknown rather than silently converted to zero
Accepted work is reconciled with spec.md and durable ADRs, then split into endpoint configuration, FreeLLMAPI integration, provenance and diversity, and zero-cost enforcement tickets
items.source: User backlog request 2026-08-20; BTN-3, BTN-14, BTN-15, BTN-35; github.com/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi
items.notes: Architecture first because this crosses configuration, provenance, cost semantics, external routing, and an existing mechanical safety constraint. Battalion already has partial local-model support through keyless-provider recognition and NodeLLMConfig.extra_params; the RFC must extend rather than replace those capabilities.

items.title: Endpoint-aware local inference configuration and setup
items.description: Extend Battalion's existing LiteLLM configuration and guided setup so per-role models can target local inference endpoints explicitly and reproducibly.
acceptance_criteria: Per-node configuration can express the model and endpoint parameters required for Ollama, LM Studio or other OpenAI-compatible localhost servers, and vLLM without hardcoding those runtimes into node implementations
battalion setup configures and preserves endpoint-aware NodeLLMConfig fields instead of reducing every role to only a normalized model string
Setup recognizes supported local and keyless targets without requesting irrelevant provider credentials, while bearer tokens and other secrets remain outside repository configuration

Connectivity validation checks each distinct effective inference target needed to prove the saved configuration; a shared provider name does not suppress validation of a different endpoint or model target
Driver and Reviewer diversity validation continues to operate on the canonical identity contract accepted by BTN-51
Endpoint URLs and non-secret settings may be persisted with explicit local or remote classification, while existing plain provider/model configurations remain backwards-compatible

Automated tests cover Ollama-style local inference, OpenAI-compatible localhost inference, unavailable endpoints, preserved existing configuration, distinct targets sharing a provider, and mixed local and remote role configurations
items.source: BTN-15 extension; BTN-51
items.notes: setup.py already treats Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio, and local providers as keyless, and NodeLLMConfig.extra_params already reaches LiteLLM. The current gaps are that run_setup persists only model strings and connectivity validation deduplicates by provider rather than effective target.

items.title: FreeLLMAPI optional inference backend
items.description: Support a user-operated FreeLLMAPI instance as an optional OpenAI-compatible inference source while keeping Battalion responsible for role, model, diversity, cost, and failure policy.
acceptance_criteria: Battalion can configure a FreeLLMAPI /v1 endpoint and obtain its bearer credential from the approved secret boundary through the endpoint-aware model configuration path
Architect, Driver, Reviewer, and Refactorer can independently select concrete FreeLLMAPI model families without node-specific integration code
Setup performs a minimal endpoint and requested-model availability check before saving validated configuration without persisting the bearer credential
Battalion does not depend on FreeLLMAPI-specific graph, workflow, role, smart-routing, prompt-transformation, or application policy
Opaque auto, profile, fusion, or equivalent virtual routes cannot satisfy Driver and Reviewer diversity unless BTN-51 defines a mechanically verifiable identity contract for them
Concrete model families may use provider-level failover only when it preserves the configured model and cost-policy identity and emits sufficient resolution evidence
FreeLLMAPI unavailability, malformed routing evidence, exhausted provider capacity, and upstream failures surface through Battalion's existing infra-failure and interrupt boundary

Tests use mocked or disposable local endpoints, require no external network or paid key, and cover model discovery, authentication failure, concrete routing, unavailable capacity, and compatible failure responses
items.source: BTN-51; github.com/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi
items.notes: FreeLLMAPI currently exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, concrete and virtual routes, provider failover, and routed-provider response metadata. Its free-tier catalog and upstream availability can change, and its documentation characterizes the project as personal-experimentation infrastructure rather than a production SLA.

items.title: Resolved inference identity and model-diversity provenance
items.description: Extend durable LLM-call evidence so Battalion records requested and effective inference identity and can demonstrate that model-diversity rules remain true across local endpoints and proxies.
acceptance_criteria: Durable execution evidence distinguishes requested model, resolved or response model when available, backend and endpoint classification, and routed provider when reliably reported
Existing token, monetary cost, currency, and cost-source evidence remains backwards-compatible, including explicit unknown monetary evidence
A local call is durably identifiable as local inference rather than appearing only as an arbitrary OpenAI-compatible model string
A FreeLLMAPI call preserves the Battalion-requested concrete model and routed provider/model metadata such as X-Routed-Via when available without fabricating absent evidence
BTN-14 configuration validation is reconciled with the new identity model so differently named aliases cannot trivially masquerade as independent Driver and Reviewer models
If runtime evidence contradicts the configured diversity assumption, Battalion records the contradiction and follows the failure or interrupt behavior accepted by BTN-51
Historical execution records remain readable through an explicit migration or compatibility path
BTN-44 analytics consumes the new typed fields without inferring provider, endpoint, or model identity from display strings
items.source: BTN-14, BTN-19, BTN-35, BTN-44; BTN-51
items.notes: BTN-14 currently compares configured model strings, while LLM-call evidence records the response model plus token and cost information. That is adequate for direct providers but not a robust provenance contract for routed endpoints.

items.title: Zero-cost execution policy and enforcement
items.description: Add a user-selectable inference-cost policy that can mechanically prevent Battalion runs from intentionally using paid inference while preserving explicit unknown-cost semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Battalion implements the inference policies accepted by BTN-51, including at minimum local-only and free-only
local-only rejects every configured inference target not verifiably classified as local before graph execution begins
free-only rejects targets known to require paid inference and never silently falls back from a free or local target to a paid provider
Unknown cost or free-tier status follows BTN-51's explicit policy and is never treated as zero merely because a provider or proxy omitted monetary evidence
Provider-reported non-zero cost under a zero-cost policy is recorded durably and triggers the policy-violation or interrupt behavior accepted by BTN-51
Retry, model routing, and provider failover cannot cross the configured cost-policy boundary
Cost policy is visible through application and CLI inspection and is durable run configuration and evidence rather than an ephemeral setup preference
Existing turn-budget interrupt semantics remain separate from monetary inference policy

Tests cover local-only success, remote rejection under local-only, verified zero-cost remote success, forbidden paid fallback, unknown cost, reported non-zero cost, resume, and mixed-role configurations
items.source: BTN-8, BTN-27, BTN-35; BTN-51
items.notes: Do not overload budget_limit, which tracks graph-run turns rather than money. FreeLLMAPI is one possible inference source, not the definition of free-only policy; the policy must remain valid if that external project or its provider catalog changes.

items.title: Desktop visual system and brand assets
items.description: Apply the accepted ui/mockup visual tokens, typography, and application icon to the production PySide6 client without changing its application-boundary behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The production desktop uses the mockup's IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono typography, charcoal surface hierarchy, restrained blue accent, compact spacing, borders, and control states
Font files are bundled under their license and load without requiring system installation or runtime network access
The supplied Battalion icon is used for the window and frozen Windows executable
Source, installed-package, and frozen-build paths include the required visual assets reproducibly
Existing keyboard navigation, accessible names, human actions, and application-boundary authority remain unchanged
Automated tests cover font registration, icon discovery, style tokens, package data, and deployment configuration, with a rendered screenshot reviewed before completion
items.source: User-provided ui/mockup visual design and assets, 2026-08-20
items.notes: Completed 2026-08-20. The BTN-52 labels inside the mockup are illustrative content only; canonical BTN-52 remains the endpoint-aware local inference ticket. The production client now registers bundled IBM Plex Sans and Mono faces, applies the supplied charcoal, border, spacing, control-state, and blue-accent tokens, displays the Battalion mark, and uses the supplied icon for its window and generated Windows executable. The OFL license and assets are included in Python package data and the frozen distribution configuration. Existing accessible names and application-boundary behavior are unchanged. The current product specification, workflows, and screen contract in docs/ui were reconciled with BTN-42, BTN-43, and BTN-56. Focused validation passed 18 tests, the complete offline suite passed 419 tests, and the offscreen production render was visually reviewed. No native Nuitka build was run for this presentation-only change.

items.title: GitHub Pages product showcase and visual assets
items.description: Refresh Battalion's public GitHub Pages experience with truthful production screenshots, the accepted Battalion mark and icons, and a concise visual introduction to the shipped operator workflow.
acceptance_criteria: The Pages landing experience uses the canonical Battalion mark and an appropriate favicon or application icon from the BTN-56 asset set rather than introducing an unrelated or divergent brand copy

The site presents reviewed screenshots of the production PySide6 client covering representative shipped Work, run detail or History, interrupt or human-action, and Intel experiences without depicting mockup-only or unshipped behavior

Screenshots are generated from deterministic credential-free fixture or demo data, contain no secrets, provider credentials, personal paths, or misleading live-service claims, and have a documented refresh procedure

Each visual has useful alternative text and a concise caption or surrounding explanation, remains readable on narrow and wide layouts, and does not replace the text path to the same documentation or workflow

The landing copy explains Battalion's human-directed Architect to Driver to Reviewer to Refactorer workflow, links to the current specification, plan, ADR index, and operator documentation, and clearly labels future roadmap behavior as unshipped
Published raster assets are appropriately sized and compressed, retain legible text at their rendered dimensions, and do not materially regress the Pages landing page load or repository size

scripts/build_pages.py explicitly stages every new public document and asset, focused tests validate the publication allowlist, rewritten links, image and favicon destinations, and the staged Pages output contains no broken local references
The final staged Pages site is visually reviewed at desktop and narrow viewport widths before the ticket is marked done
items.source: User backlog request 2026-08-20; BTN-18, BTN-42, BTN-43, BTN-56
items.notes: Completed on codex/BTN-57 on 2026-08-20; the live GitHub Pages site updates only after merge to main. The landing page reuses the BTN-56 mark and favicon, explains the shipped human-directed role loop, distinguishes roadmap behavior, and links the specification, plan, ADR index, and published operator documentation. Three reviewed production PySide6 captures cover Work plus human action, History execution evidence, and Intel review. scripts/capture_pages_screenshots.py renders fixed fictional in-memory projections with the public showcase-operator identity and no provider, credential, developer run-state, Git, or network access; docs/ui/showcase.md documents refresh and review. The explicit Pages allowlist stages the layout, stylesheet, operator documents, brand files, and optimized 1380x860 PNGs (each below 150 KB), with tests covering destinations, link rewriting, local references, dimensions, size, and fixture safety. Focused validation passed 22 tests; the complete offline suite passed 423 tests. The staged landing page was visually reviewed in the in-app browser at 1440x1000 and 390x844 with all images loaded, useful alt text, responsive one-column behavior, and no horizontal page overflow.

items.title: Human identity, authority, assignment, and collaboration RFC
items.description: Define Battalion's durable human identity and collaboration model before the existing actor evidence from human actions spreads into additional persistence, UI, assignment, or remote-client contracts. Separate identity, authentication, authorization, membership, assignment, and observed social or expertise evidence.
acceptance_criteria: The RFC defines a stable Actor identity contract for humans and system actors without assuming that display name, GitHub login, email address, operating-system username, or authentication credential is the durable identity

Identity, authentication, and authorization are explicitly separate concepts: Battalion can identify a local actor before remote authentication exists, and authentication alone does not grant project authority

The RFC defines project membership and human capabilities such as inspect, operate, approve, assign, and administer without conflating them with Battalion AI roles such as Architect, Driver, Reviewer, and Refactorer
The RFC defines the distinction between actor, operator, assignee, owner, reviewer or approval authority, and observer where those concepts are materially different
Existing BTN-43 HumanActionRecord and HumanIntervention evidence is reconciled with the Actor model, including compatibility for historical string actor values

The RFC defines assignment and handoff semantics for Tickets and Runs, including assigned_by, assignment time, reassignment history, and what responsibility transfers versus what historical provenance remains immutable

Authorization rules are defined for existing human actions including interrupt resolution, resume, bounded Correction, Design decision, Recon promotion or rejection, cancellation, and future assignment operations
The design preserves the shared application boundary so CLI, desktop, future web or mobile clients cannot bypass authorization by mutating RunState, Intel, worker metadata, or project files directly

Authentication providers, accounts, hosted identity services, OAuth, remote session management, and organization administration remain implementation-deferred unless required to establish a stable boundary
Empirically inferred collaboration or expertise evidence is explicitly non-authoritative: social-graph evidence may recommend a person but cannot grant capabilities or approval authority
The RFC identifies migration, specification, ADR, persistence, application, desktop, authentication, and collaboration follow-up tickets without implementing them
items.source: BTN-43 durable human-action evidence; collaboration requirements; future multi-client and remote-worker architecture
items.notes: Completed 2026-08-21. The human operator accepted RFC-0007 and ADR-0026. They define opaque durable human and system Actor identity; separate authentication, membership, authorization, assignment, Ticket ownership, and non-authoritative collaboration evidence; preserve literal legacy actor strings; require a distinct resolve-interrupt capability; establish an Actor-credited one-time FTUE bootstrap; and retain the shared application boundary. Runtime implementation remains BTN-59 through BTN-62. Validation on the BTN-58 feature branch: 6 focused Pages tests and the complete offline suite of 423 tests passed.

items.title: Durable Actor identity and local operator provenance
items.description: Implement the accepted Actor identity contract and migrate current human-action attribution from free-form actor strings to durable actor references while preserving local-first operation and historical compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: Battalion defines a versioned Actor contract with a stable actor_id, actor kind, display name, creation provenance, and only the identity fields accepted by BTN-58
A project can establish or select a local human actor without OAuth, a hosted account service, or network access

Project first-time-use creates or selects the first local human Actor and durably credits the one-time bootstrap membership and administration event to that Actor without treating an operating-system username as actor identity

HumanActionRecord, HumanIntervention, interrupt resolution, Recon review decisions, and other existing human-attributed evidence reference durable actor identity according to the BTN-58 migration contract
Historical records containing only the pre-BTN-59 string actor remain readable and are presented as legacy attribution without inventing a durable identity that was not recorded
Changing an actor's display name does not rewrite historical action evidence or change actor_id
System-generated actions can be attributed to explicitly typed system actors rather than masquerading as human users
Actor lookup and inspection are exposed through the shared application query boundary rather than direct presentation-layer persistence access
CLI and desktop source execution continue to work for a single local operator without requiring authentication infrastructure
Tests cover actor creation or selection, stable identity, display-name change, legacy attribution, system actors, malformed identity data, and persistence round trips
items.source: BTN-58; BTN-43 HumanActionRecord and HumanIntervention provenance
items.notes: Completed 2026-08-21. Added the versioned project-local human/system Actor contract, atomic one-time offline FTUE bootstrap evidence, durable local selection, shared application bootstrap/inspection queries, and actor_id attribution for RunState human actions, interventions, interrupt resolution, Recon decisions, and accepted Intel. Literal pre-BTN-59 strings remain readable and render as legacy attribution; display snapshots remain immutable when Actor names change. CLI, desktop, and detached workers use the selected local Actor without OS usernames or authentication infrastructure. Validation: complete offline suite of 434 tests passed. OAuth, passwords, cloud accounts, remote login, capability enforcement, assignment, and ownership remain outside BTN-59.

items.title: Project membership and capability authorization
items.description: Implement project-scoped membership and capability checks for human operations so durable actor identity is mechanically connected to the authority exercised through Battalion's application boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Project membership binds an Actor to one project and grants only capabilities accepted by BTN-58, including inspect, operate, resolve-interrupt, approve, assign, and administer
Human capabilities are represented independently from AI execution roles and cannot cause a human to become an Architect, Driver, Reviewer, or Refactorer node
Every state-changing human application command identifies the requesting actor and mechanically checks the capability required for that action before mutation occurs
Existing BTN-43 operations including interrupt resolution, resume, Correction, Design decision, Recon review, and cancellation are mapped to explicit capability requirements
Denied actions produce typed application failures and durable security or operator evidence where required by BTN-58 without partially mutating RunState, Intel, worker state, or assignment state
Read-only inspection behavior for non-members, observers, or unauthorized actors follows the explicit BTN-58 policy rather than presentation-client assumptions
Configured local unauthenticated read-only inspection runs as an explicit inspect-only system Actor and is never attributed to the human operator
Membership or capability changes do not retroactively alter the authority evidence attached to prior human actions
The application boundary remains the single authorization enforcement point shared by CLI, desktop, and future presentation clients
A backwards-compatible single-local-operator configuration remains available without requiring an external identity provider
Tests cover permitted and denied actions, capability changes, cross-project isolation, legacy/local operation, and attempts to bypass authorization through presentation adapters
items.source: BTN-58; BTN-30 application authority boundary; BTN-43 human actions
items.notes: Prefer capability grants over a premature fixed RBAC hierarchy. Named human roles may later be convenience bundles of capabilities, but authorization must not depend on presentation-only labels.

items.title: Ticket and Run assignment, ownership, reassignment, and handoff
items.description: Add durable human assignment and handoff for Tickets and Runs plus durable Ticket ownership so responsibility and accountability can transfer between authorized actors without transcript injection or loss of execution provenance.
acceptance_criteria: Battalion represents current assignment separately from immutable assignment history for the target types accepted by BTN-58
Battalion represents current Ticket ownership separately from immutable ownership history and separately from Ticket or Run assignment
An assignment records target identity, assignee actor_id, assigning actor_id, timestamp, and any bounded reason or handoff context accepted by the RFC
Only actors with the required assignment capability may assign or reassign work, and an assignee must satisfy the target project's membership requirements
Reassignment changes current responsibility but never rewrites the actor attribution of prior human actions, node executions, decisions, or earlier assignments

Ticket ownership transfer records the owner actor_id, authorizing actor_id, timestamp, bounded reason, and superseded ownership event without granting capabilities, implying assignment, or rewriting prior ownership

A Run can be handed from one actor to another while preserving its canonical run identity, durable RunState, execution evidence, pending interrupt, worker evidence, Intel references, and project identity
Opening an assigned Run does not require replaying or injecting another user's conversation history; the durable Run and repository evidence remain the handoff source of truth
The application layer exposes assignment and Ticket ownership inspection and mutation operations for presentation clients with typed authorization and conflict failures
Desktop presentation exposes current assignment, Ticket ownership, and their histories and provides mutation controls only where the active actor is authorized
Concurrent or stale reassignment and ownership-transfer attempts cannot silently overwrite a newer responsibility record and have explicit conflict behavior

Tests cover initial assignment, reassignment, unauthorized assignment, invalid assignee, handoff of awaiting-human and inactive runs, assignment-history preservation, initial Ticket ownership, ownership transfer and history, assignment-independent ownership, unauthorized ownership transfer, and stale-write conflicts
items.source: BTN-58; collaboration handoff requirement; durable Run identity from BTN-32
items.notes: This implements collaboration semantics, not networking. Bob and Alice may initially operate the same local/project storage. Cross-machine synchronization, hosted storage, notifications, and remote workers are separate future concerns.

items.title: Authentication and remote identity boundary RFC
items.description: Define how an external or remote presentation client proves that it represents a durable Battalion Actor without coupling Actor identity or project authorization to any one authentication provider.
acceptance_criteria: The RFC defines the trust boundary between an authenticated session or credential and Battalion's durable Actor identity
External identities such as GitHub, Microsoft or Entra, operating-system identity, and future Battalion-hosted accounts are evaluated as identity links rather than replacements for actor_id
The design defines account linking, unlinking, duplicate or conflicting external identities, disabled identities, actor deactivation, and credential rotation without rewriting historical provenance
Authentication success and authorization are explicitly separate; proving an identity does not grant project membership or capabilities
Desktop-local operation remains possible without requiring a remote authentication service
The RFC compares authentication needs for local desktop, web, mobile, remote worker, and shared-server deployment without requiring all of those deployment models to be implemented
Session lifetime, token or credential storage, logout or revocation, replay resistance, transport security, and secret boundaries are defined at the level necessary for future implementation
Machine and worker identities are distinguished from human Actor identity so a remote execution host cannot impersonate the human who authorized work
The design identifies any application protocol, server, persistence, UI, deployment, and security implementation tickets required for an accepted remote-client architecture
No authentication provider, Azure deployment, web client, mobile client, or remote worker implementation is authorized by this RFC ticket itself
items.source: BTN-58; future web/mobile presentation clients and remote-worker deployment
items.notes: Keep authentication provider-neutral. Local Actor identity should remain useful even if Battalion never gains a hosted account service. Azure, GitHub OAuth, Entra, passkeys, or another mechanism should be implementation choices behind the accepted identity boundary.

items.title: Actor identity and external identity mappings
items.description: Introduce Actor as a durable Battalion identity and model external identities as provider- and integration-scoped mappings so collaboration, assignment, notifications, authorization, and external-system identity can share one canonical domain identity.
acceptance_criteria: Actors have stable canonical identity independent of usernames, email addresses, provider accounts, or external systems
An Actor may have zero or more external identities
Each external identity identifies an integration_id, provider, and external subject
The same Actor may have identities in multiple instances of the same provider, such as multiple Discord servers, GitHub organizations, or future Slack workspaces
An integration_id plus external subject cannot ambiguously resolve to multiple Actors
External identity records contain identifiers and metadata but never provider credentials or secrets
Linking, unlinking, malformed mappings, duplicate mappings, persistence, and migration behavior are covered by automated tests
items.source: User integration architecture discussion 2026-08-21
items.notes: Actor is a Battalion domain identity, not an alias for a user account in any external provider. External identities are scoped to configured integration instances so provider identities remain unambiguous.

items.title: Actor authorization and external-action authority
items.description: Define and implement the authority boundary between resolved Actor identity and permitted Battalion operations, including human-controlled actions originating from desktop, CLI, REST, notifications, and future bidirectional integrations.
acceptance_criteria: Resolving an external identity to an Actor does not itself authorize an operation
Operation-level authorization exists for human-controlled application commands including approve, resume, cancel, inspect, and reassign where those operations are supported
Authorization semantics are independent of whether an action originates from the desktop application, CLI, REST API, or an external integration
Project, Run, ownership, assignment, and role information may participate in authorization without provider-specific concepts entering the core domain model
Denied operations produce explicit inspectable outcomes and do not mutate Run state
The design defines future organization, project, and Actor policy precedence without requiring organization-level configuration in this ticket
Security-sensitive authority changes cannot be approved solely by an AI model or an external identity mapping
items.source: Battalion AI philosophy; User integration architecture discussion 2026-08-21
items.notes: Identity and authority are deliberately separate. External systems may establish who is acting, but Battalion remains responsible for deciding what that Actor is allowed to do.

items.title: Transport-neutral integration capability architecture
items.description: Define Battalion external integrations around bounded capability contracts rather than vendor APIs, MCP tools, or transport-specific clients, with providers and transports remaining interchangeable beneath Battalion-owned policy.
acceptance_criteria: The architecture defines initial capability contracts for WorkSource, KnowledgeSource, RepositoryService, Notification, OutboundEventSink, and HumanInteraction
Capability contracts contain no MCP-, REST-, GitHub-, Discord-, email-, Jira-, Slack-, or other provider-specific concepts
The architecture explicitly separates Battalion capability, provider adapter, transport, and external system
Initial transport taxonomy includes native or local, HTTP or REST, webhook, MCP, and protocol-specific transports such as SMTP
Graph nodes cannot obtain unrestricted raw external clients or arbitrary MCP tool collections through this architecture
Each capability defines allowed callers, data boundaries, side-effect semantics, failure semantics, and authority expectations

KnowledgeSource and RepositoryService may remain unimplemented but their boundaries are defined sufficiently to prevent later architectural collision, including with a future local VersionControl engine abstraction
BTN-46 is reconciled so future plugins may implement these contracts but plugin support is neither required nor privileged
items.source: User integration architecture discussion 2026-08-21; BTN-46
items.notes: Completed 2026-08-21. Accepted RFC-0006 and ADR-0025 define WorkSource, KnowledgeSource, RepositoryService, Notification, OutboundEventSink, and HumanInteraction as Battalion-owned capability contracts above provider adapters and least-authority native/local, HTTP/REST, webhook, MCP, and protocol-specific transports. MCP and future plugins are optional and unprivileged. RepositoryService is deliberately separate from a future local VersionControl engine abstraction. No runtime integration behavior ships in this ticket; delivery remains BTN-66 through BTN-80. Focused Pages validation passed 6 tests and the complete offline suite passed 423 tests.

items.title: Portable integration configuration and secret indirection
items.description: Add portable configuration for named integrations, providers, transports, capability assignments, and non-secret settings while keeping credentials outside repository-shareable configuration.
acceptance_criteria: Configuration can assign named provider and transport combinations to Battalion capability surfaces
Integration instances have stable integration_id values suitable for Actor external identity mappings and durable provenance
Non-secret integration configuration may be checked into or passed with a Battalion project
Credentials and secrets are represented only by approved references and are resolved outside repository configuration
Configuration supports future organization, project, and Actor precedence while implementing only currently required layers
Actor-level preferences cannot enable providers or capabilities forbidden by higher-level project policy
Existing Battalion configuration remains backwards-compatible
Configuration export and sharing exclude secret material
items.source: User integration architecture discussion 2026-08-21
items.notes: A portable configuration should communicate which integrations a project expects without carrying credentials required to access them.

items.title: Integration adapter runtime and transport boundary
items.description: Implement the runtime boundary that resolves configured Battalion capabilities to approved provider adapters and transports without exposing unrestricted external clients to graph nodes or application callers.
acceptance_criteria: Application and graph code request external behavior only through Battalion capability interfaces
Provider adapters receive only explicitly bound transport capabilities needed for their declared operation
Unsupported provider and transport combinations fail during validation where they can be detected before Run execution
Timeout, cancellation, transport failure, malformed responses, and unavailable integrations have typed failure semantics
Adapter or transport failure cannot silently corrupt graph or durable Run state
Transport implementations cannot broaden the authority of the capability operation invoking them
Automated tests use deterministic fakes and require no live provider credentials or network services
items.source: BTN-60; User integration architecture discussion 2026-08-21
items.notes: This runtime is the structural boundary that prevents integration transport details from leaking into graph logic.

items.title: Integration operation policy enforcement
items.description: Enforce Battalion-owned operation policy between capability requests and external side effects so provider and transport capabilities remain least-authority and external systems cannot bypass application authorization.
acceptance_criteria: Policies operate on Battalion operations such as work.read, work.comment, notification.send, and event.publish rather than transport tool names
Policy enforcement is identical whether an operation is implemented through REST, MCP, SMTP, webhook, SDK, or another transport
Actor authorization is evaluated for externally originated commands before any Run mutation
Capability grants remain least-authority and adapters cannot invoke external operations outside the approved Battalion operation
Read authority and mutation or side-effect authority can be configured and evaluated independently
Policy denial is distinguishable from provider, authentication, and transport failure
No AI prompt or model instruction is relied upon as the enforcement mechanism
Automated tests demonstrate that raw provider capability cannot bypass denied Battalion operations
items.source: Battalion AI philosophy; BTN-2 structural scope pattern; User integration architecture discussion 2026-08-21
items.notes: The policy boundary preserves the same structural-enforcement principle Battalion already uses for node write scopes.

items.title: Integration health and capability validation
items.description: Validate integration configuration, credentials, reachability, compatibility, and advertised capabilities before Runs depend upon external services, with typed health and degradation state.
acceptance_criteria: Every configured integration exposes typed configuration and health status
Validation distinguishes configuration, authentication, connectivity, compatibility, and advertised-capability failures
MCP capability or tool drift can be detected without embedding static MCP tool names in graph-node prompts
Deterministic REST, webhook, SMTP, and similar integrations receive equivalent validation where practical
Integration health is inspectable through the shared application boundary for CLI and desktop consumers
Unavailable optional integrations can degrade independently rather than automatically failing unrelated Runs
Required integration failures block the dependent operation explicitly rather than surfacing as unrelated graph failures
Validation and health tests require no live credentials
items.source: Regiment MCP drift findings; User integration architecture discussion 2026-08-21
items.notes: Generalizes Regiment's MCP drift lesson into transport-neutral Battalion health validation.

items.title: External side-effect evidence and idempotent delivery
items.description: Persist inspectable evidence for external operations and make side-effect delivery replay-safe across retries, resume, crashes, and duplicate event processing.
acceptance_criteria: Every externally visible attempted side effect receives a stable logical operation or event ID
Durable records include Run identity, Actor identity where applicable, capability, integration, operation, timestamp, attempt information, and outcome
Retry and resume semantics prevent one logical operation from unintentionally producing duplicate Slack-like messages, emails, webhooks, GitHub comments, or equivalent external effects
Provider idempotency mechanisms are used when available but Battalion retains its own stable logical operation identity
Failed external delivery remains distinguishable from failed workflow execution
Audit records exclude secrets and avoid persisting unnecessary copies of external payload contents
Existing durable event identity and duplicate-delivery semantics are reused or reconciled rather than introducing a competing event model
Automated tests cover crash-before-response, timeout-after-remote-success, retry, resume, and duplicate-processing scenarios
items.source: BTN-19, BTN-36; User integration architecture discussion 2026-08-21
items.notes: External side effects must remain auditable and safe to retry because Battalion Runs are durable and resumable.

items.title: WorkSource abstraction and local backlog provider
items.description: Decouple Run intake from Battalion's local backlog representation by introducing a normalized WorkSource and WorkItem contract, with the existing local backlog as the first backwards-compatible provider.
acceptance_criteria: A Run can originate from a normalized WorkItem supplied through a configured WorkSource
The existing Battalion backlog remains usable through a local WorkSource provider without regressing current CLI or application behavior
Canonical Battalion Run identity remains separate from external work-item identity
Source integration, external identifier, source revision or update evidence when available, and retrieval provenance are retained durably
Work-item reads and external mutations are distinct WorkSource operations with separately enforceable authority
Graph nodes do not directly invoke GitHub, Jira, local-backlog, or other provider APIs
The contract supports future GitHub Issues, Jira, Azure DevOps, and other providers without provider-specific fields entering core graph state
Automated tests cover local WorkSource intake and source provenance
items.source: User integration architecture discussion 2026-08-21
items.notes: The local backlog becomes a provider of Battalion's WorkSource contract rather than the universal definition of external work.

items.title: GitHub Issues WorkSource adapter
items.description: Implement GitHub Issues as Battalion's first external WorkSource so Battalion can consume and update real Issues from its own repository while preserving transport neutrality, policy, provenance, and idempotency.
acceptance_criteria: A configured GitHub Issue can be normalized into a Battalion WorkItem and used to start a Run

Repository identity, issue number, external URL or reference, source update evidence, labels, assignee information where relevant, and retrieval provenance are retained without becoming provider-specific core Run fields
Battalion can use an Issue from the Battalion repository itself as a WorkSource input
Permitted GitHub comments, state changes, labels, or other accepted mutations pass through Battalion integration policy rather than direct graph-node GitHub access
External mutations participate in Battalion idempotency and side-effect evidence
Authentication uses the approved secret boundary and credentials are absent from portable integration configuration
The adapter boundary remains compatible with REST, GraphQL, SDK, or other deterministic GitHub transport implementation without changing WorkSource
Automated tests use deterministic fakes or mocked GitHub responses and require no live GitHub credentials
items.source: User dogfooding decision 2026-08-21; github.com/lrburkholder/battalion
items.notes: GitHub Issues is intentionally the first external WorkSource because Battalion can immediately use its own repository issues to build Battalion. Jira remains a future second-provider validation.

items.title: Versioned outbound event sink contract
items.description: Define and implement a generic outbound event-sink capability so external automation can consume selected Battalion domain events without being treated as a human notification channel or gaining mutation authority.
acceptance_criteria: Battalion can publish selected domain events through configured OutboundEventSink providers
Each outbound event envelope includes stable event ID, event type, schema version, occurrence timestamp, Run or project provenance where applicable, and bounded event data
Initial supported external events include human_interrupt, run_failed, and run_completed
Publishing an event does not grant the receiving system authority to mutate Battalion
Event schema evolution and compatibility rules are documented and tested
Payload minimization is explicit and arbitrary transcripts, prompts, source code, model context, and secrets are excluded by default
Outbound event delivery uses BTN-65 retry, audit, and idempotency semantics
Event consumers remain independent of any particular provider such as Zapier or Discord
items.source: User Zapier and notification architecture discussion 2026-08-21
items.notes: OutboundEventSink is broader than Notification. Machine automation may consume Run events even when no human needs to be notified.

items.title: Generic outbound HTTP webhook adapter
items.description: Implement a generic HTTP webhook OutboundEventSink so Battalion can integrate with Zapier, internal automation, custom services, and similar systems without provider-specific application code.
acceptance_criteria: Configured outbound events can be delivered as HTTP POST requests to a webhook endpoint
Endpoint URL and non-secret request configuration are portable while credentials and authorization material use approved secret indirection
Configuration can select which event types are delivered to a particular sink
Timeout, retry, non-success HTTP response, malformed configuration, unavailable endpoint, and cancellation behavior are explicit and tested
Retries retain the same logical Battalion event identity
Webhook payloads use the versioned outbound event envelope from BTN-68
No Zapier-specific or other automation-vendor-specific code is required
Automated tests use a local or fake HTTP endpoint and require no external network access
items.source: User Zapier discussion 2026-08-21
items.notes: This should provide useful Zapier and internal-automation integration without a native Zapier application. Add provider-specific integration only when generic HTTP demonstrably fails a concrete use case.

items.title: Actor-targeted notification routing
items.description: Route human notifications by Battalion Actor identity rather than raw provider destinations, resolving configured external identities and channel policy only at the notification boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Notification requests target Actor IDs or explicitly defined Actor groups rather than raw email addresses, Discord IDs, provider user IDs, or device tokens
The router resolves Actor destinations through external identity mappings and the selected configured integration
An Actor may have different destinations for multiple instances of the same provider
Missing destination, disabled channel, unavailable integration, policy denial, and failed delivery are distinct outcomes
One logical notification may fan out to multiple configured channels without creating unrelated notification identities
Project defaults and permitted Actor preferences can determine channel selection without allowing Actor preferences to bypass higher-level policy
Notification failure does not corrupt, dismiss, or silently resolve the underlying HumanInterrupt
Notification routing participates in BTN-65 audit and idempotency semantics
items.source: User actor-targeted notification discussion 2026-08-21
items.notes: The graph should express notify Actor X, not send to provider destination Y.

items.title: Deterministic email notification adapter
items.description: Implement actor-targeted email as a deterministic notification provider using an explicitly configured mail transport without making email an interactive Run-control surface.
acceptance_criteria: The adapter resolves an Actor's email identity through the external identity model
SMTP or another explicitly selected deterministic mail transport is configured beneath the Notification capability without email concepts entering graph logic
Credentials remain outside portable project configuration
HumanInterrupt notifications can include bounded Run identifier, work-item identifier, phase, reason, and a safe route back to Battalion
Email delivery is notification-only and cannot implicitly approve, resume, cancel, or mutate a Run
Duplicate suppression, missing recipient, authentication failure, timeout, unavailable transport, and retry behavior are tested
Email contents exclude unnecessary prompts, transcripts, source code, model context, and secrets
Delivery evidence uses BTN-65 semantics

items.notes: Email is intentionally a notification surface, not a command or approval surface.

items.title: Push notification provider contract and first adapter
items.description: Define actor-targeted push notification semantics and implement one bounded provider or transport without coupling Battalion's domain model to a particular mobile notification vendor.
acceptance_criteria: Push destinations are external Actor identities associated with a configured integration
The ticket documents and selects one bounded initial provider or transport rather than introducing a provider-neutral abstraction with no proof implementation
Device or provider tokens are treated as sensitive and are not stored in repository-shareable configuration
Push payloads are deliberately minimal and do not include arbitrary source, prompts, transcripts, secrets, or model context
Push notifications are outbound notification-only in the initial implementation
Multiple devices, stale endpoints, revoked destinations, partial fan-out failure, retry, and duplicate delivery are handled explicitly
Provider-specific concepts remain below the Notification capability boundary
Automated tests require no live push service credentials
items.source: User notification channel discussion 2026-08-21
items.notes: The implementation should select the simplest zero-cost provider suitable for Battalion dogfooding when this ticket is started. Do not invent a mobile dependency before a concrete client exists.

items.title: MCP transport implementation
items.description: Implement MCP as one optional transport beneath Battalion integration capability contracts, with capability discovery, validation, least-authority binding, failure handling, and audit semantics owned by Battalion.
acceptance_criteria: Battalion can connect to explicitly configured MCP servers and inspect their advertised tools or capabilities
MCP tools are exposed only through approved Battalion provider adapters and graph nodes never receive an unrestricted MCP server tool collection
MCP server names and tool names do not leak into core capability interfaces or durable workflow semantics
Server connection, authentication, timeout, disconnect, malformed response, cancellation, and capability drift are handled through common integration runtime and health semantics
MCP cannot bypass BTN-63 operation policy or Actor authorization
MCP-backed side effects participate in BTN-65 audit and idempotency evidence
A deterministic fake MCP server validates connection, discovery, allowed-tool binding, denied-tool access, drift, failure, and retry without external credentials
No real provider integration is required merely to justify MCP's existence as a supported transport
items.source: Regiment MCP experience; User integration architecture discussion 2026-08-21
items.notes: MCP is intentionally optional and unprivileged. The first real MCP-backed provider should be added only when MCP is the appropriate transport for a concrete use case.

items.title: Discord human-interrupt notification adapter
items.description: Implement Discord as the first dogfood human-interrupt notification channel, initially using deterministic webhook-based delivery and preserving a path to Actor-targeted bot delivery only if needed later.
acceptance_criteria: A configured Discord integration can receive HumanInterrupt notifications from Battalion
The initial implementation uses the simplest deterministic Discord webhook path that satisfies Battalion dogfooding rather than introducing MCP or a bot unnecessarily
Notifications include bounded Run identifier, work-item identifier, phase, interrupt reason, and a safe route back to Battalion
Discord notification delivery is outbound-only and Discord messages or replies cannot mutate a Run in this ticket
Discord-specific endpoint or destination information remains below the Notification or OutboundEventSink boundary and does not enter graph-node prompts or workflow state
Webhook authentication or secret URL material is handled through the approved secret boundary and is absent from shareable project configuration
Retry, duplicate delivery, unavailable Discord, invalid configuration, and delivery failure use common BTN-65 semantics
Automated tests use deterministic HTTP fakes and require no live Discord server
items.source: User dogfooding decision 2026-08-21
items.notes: Discord replaces Slack as the initial dogfood notification proof. This ticket does not depend on MCP; do not manufacture an MCP dependency where deterministic HTTP is sufficient.

items.title: External integration dogfood: Battalion builds Battalion
items.description: Validate the external integration architecture end to end by using Battalion against a real Battalion GitHub Issue, delivering a real human-interrupt notification, resolving the interrupt through Battalion, and publishing configured completion evidence back to GitHub.
acceptance_criteria: A real GitHub Issue from the Battalion repository is selected or created as the source work item for the dogfood scenario
Battalion imports the Issue through the GitHub Issues WorkSource rather than by manually copying its contents into Run state
The resulting Run preserves GitHub source identity and integration provenance
The Run reaches or deliberately invokes a real HumanInterrupt through Battalion's normal interrupt mechanism
The responsible Battalion Actor is resolved and receives the configured Discord and/or email notification through Actor-targeted notification routing
The human resolves the interrupt through Battalion's authoritative application surface rather than by treating an outbound notification as implicit approval
The Run resumes after the human decision and continues through its normal graph semantics
On configured completion, Battalion performs an authorized GitHub Issue update or comment through WorkSource policy rather than direct graph-node provider access
Run history contains inspectable external-operation evidence covering source retrieval, notification attempts and outcomes, human resolution, and GitHub mutation without exposing secrets
Repeating or resuming the scenario does not duplicate already-completed logical external side effects

Automated integration coverage remains credential-free and uses deterministic provider fakes, while this ticket's final acceptance exercise uses the real Battalion GitHub repository and at least one real configured notification channel
Any architectural special case required specifically for GitHub, Discord, email, REST, or MCP is treated as a design finding and reconciled before this ticket is marked done
items.source: User dogfooding milestone decision 2026-08-21
items.notes: This is the architecture proof, not merely a provider demo: Battalion should use its own GitHub Issues and its own human-interrupt machinery while building Battalion. Email may participate if BTN-71 has landed, but Discord is sufficient as the required first real notification channel.

items.title: Actor notification availability and delivery policy
items.description: Add timezone-aware Actor notification availability and do-not-disturb policy so Battalion can deterministically decide whether a notification should be delivered immediately, deferred, or suppressed, with configurable treatment by notification class and durable deferred delivery.
acceptance_criteria: Each Actor may define notification availability or do-not-disturb windows using an explicitly configured timezone
Notification availability is evaluated before destination resolution and channel fan-out so Discord, email, push, and future notification providers honor the same Actor policy
DND behavior is configurable rather than implicitly meaning defer, with deliver, defer, and suppress supported as the initial policy actions
DND policy may select different actions by notification class, with initial support for informational, normal, and urgent classifications
Urgent notifications do not implicitly bypass DND; immediate delivery during DND must result from explicit configured policy

Deferred-delivery behavior is configurable, with next_available_window supported as the initial delivery mode and the configuration model allowing additional modes without redefining the notification policy contract
Deferred notifications are persisted durably and do not depend on an in-memory timer, continuously running desktop client, or continuously active Run
When a deferred notification becomes eligible for delivery, it retains its original logical notification identity and uses BTN-65 idempotency semantics
Suppressed notifications produce no external side effect but retain an inspectable durable policy outcome explaining why delivery was suppressed
DND and delivery policy affect notification delivery only and cannot resolve, cancel, approve, resume, or otherwise mutate the underlying HumanInterrupt or Run
Actor preferences cannot weaken mandatory higher-level project or future organization notification policy
Notification routing can distinguish delivered, deferred, suppressed, policy-blocked, and delivery-failed outcomes

Timezone changes, daylight-saving transitions, windows crossing midnight, overlapping windows, always-available Actors, Actors without explicit availability preferences, and malformed schedules are covered by automated tests
Policy evaluation and deferred-delivery tests are deterministic and do not require waiting for wall-clock time or accessing external notification providers
items.source: User Actor notification availability and configurable deferral policy discussion 2026-08-21
items.notes: Availability is an Actor-level Battalion policy evaluated before provider routing, not behavior implemented independently by notification adapters. Initial DND actions are deliver, defer, and suppress, and initial deferred-delivery mode is next_available_window. Digest delivery, fixed-time delivery, escalation, on-call routing, fallback Actors, and calendar-derived availability are future extensions rather than scope for this ticket.
